text:
B: Hiya! Oh, hello, love. Can you hear me all right?
A: Hello. Yeah, loud and clear. I'm Neil.
B: Joanne. I'm in Batley, West Yorkshire. Ooh, I'll be honest, when I saw your photo I thought, he looks like my Darren. It's the fleece.
A: Ha. Right. Is that good?
B: Oh, it's very good, I married him! Sorry, that's come out wrong. Anyway. Where are you?
A: Basingstoke. I've been there most of my life, near enough. Grew up in Reading.
B: And what do you do?
A: Civil engineer. Water company. Pumping stations, sewers, that sort of thing.
B: Gosh. So when it all backs up, it's you they ring.
A: Er, more or less, yeah. What about you?
B: I'm an upholsterer. I've got a little unit, I do armchairs, headboards, a few pubs and care homes.
A: Oh, that's a proper trade. Karen's got a chair from her nan that's falling to bits. I keep saying I'll have a go at it.
B: Don't you dare! Sorry, I'm only joking. But honestly, people pull the old stuff off and find horsehair and springs everywhere and then they're stuck. Bring it to somebody. Do you know what I mean?
A: Yeah, fair enough. I'll leave it then. I'm more of a fix-the-tap sort of bloke.
B: Have you got a dog? You look like you've got a dog.
A: Labrador. Bramble. I walked her along the canal just before this. What've you got?
B: Mabel, Border terrier, she's twelve. She's in her bed behind me, actually, snoring. I take her out every morning before I go to the unit, rain or shine.
A: Same. It's the best bit of the day, really, first thing. Nobody about.
B: Oh, it is. Are you a gardener, then? You seem like a gardener.
A: A bit. Raised beds. Tomatoes have done well this year, actually. And runner beans.
B: Ooh, lovely. I just do hanging baskets out the front, but in this weather I'm out with the watering can every night, the neighbours must think I'm obsessed.
A: Tomatoes are the same. You miss a day and they sulk.
B: They do sulk! Have you got holidays booked or owt?
A: Cornwall. Near Padstow. We go most summers, fifteen years now. Booked August again.
B: Oh, that's like us with Filey. You find somewhere you like, why change it?
A: That's it, really. Fish and chips on the harbour, walk the dog, home for dinner. Karen likes it.
B: Home for your tea, I'd say. We'll argue about that one.
A: Ha. We will.
B: Have you got kids, then? I saw the graduation photo.
A: Two. Both left home. Son's finishing at Nottingham. It's quiet. I miss him more than I'd say to him, probably.
B: Oh, love. Our Lewis is in Leeds, he still comes back Sundays. And I've got my mum, she's seventy-six, she's getting a bit forgetful. You worry about everybody, don't you.
A: Yeah. My mum's seventy-nine, on her own in Reading. I ring her most nights.
B: Oh, bless you. That's lovely, that is. I'm going to cry now, I'm terrible.
A: No, don't do that. Er, tell me about the chairs again. The—
